items.stem: What is the 'main idea' of a paragraph?

options.text: The most important point the paragraph is about
options.rationale: Correct: the main idea is the central point.

options.text: The longest sentence in the paragraph
options.rationale: Length does not make a sentence the main idea.

options.text: The first word of the paragraph
options.rationale: A single word is not the main idea.

options.text: Any small detail you find interesting
options.rationale: An interesting detail is not the same as the main idea.

items.explanation: Correct: the main idea is the central point.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A story says 'Sam pulled on his coat and grabbed an umbrella.' What can you infer about the weather?

options.text: It is probably cold or rainy
options.rationale: Correct: a coat and umbrella are clues to cold or wet weather.

options.text: It is a hot sunny day
options.rationale: People rarely need a coat and umbrella on a hot day.
The clues point to weather, not time of day.

items.explanation: Correct: a coat and umbrella are clues to cold or wet weather.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO strategies help you find the meaning of a new word in a passage? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Read the sentences around the word for clues
options.rationale: Correct: context clues help reveal meaning.

options.text: Look for a familiar part inside the word
options.rationale: Correct: known roots or parts give hints.
Skipping removes the context you need.

options.text: Change the word to one you like better
options.rationale: Swapping the word changes the author's meaning.

items.explanation: Correct: context clues help reveal meaning.
